newsitem.title: USA: L.A. utility selects Duke-Louis Dreyfus as partner.
newsitem.headline: L.A. utility selects Duke-Louis Dreyfus as partner.

text.p: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) selected Duke-Louis Dreyfus to be its "strategic partner" as the electricity industry enters deregulation, a spokeswoman for the municipal utility said Tuesday.
Duke-Louis Dreyfus is a joint venture of North Carolina utility Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp.
The joint venture was selected over two other finalists: a division of Enron Corp, a Houston natural gas company and power marketer; and PacifiCorp, an interstate utility based in Portland, Ore.
LADWP general manager William McCarley is expected to present the decision to the utility's board of commissioners Tuesday morning.
In a letter to the board, McCarley said Duke/Louis Dreyfus was chosen because it is the second largest power marketer in the nation and has vast expertise in all facets of the global energy market.
Although the LADWP board has jurisdiction over the selection, it has voluntarily deferred a final decision to the Los Angeles city council.
Last week, the city council declined to vote on a motion to re-open bidding for the strategic alliance, but did assign a special committee to review the matter.
Edison International, parent of Southern California Edison Co, has aggressively lobbied for the re-opening so that it can participate as a bidder.
Clarence Brown, an Edison spokesman, said Monday "We would like to be involved in the process...the other bidders have had a nine-month process."
Edison was barred from taking part in the LADWP bidding due to its status as a net generator of power, but now says plans to divest most of its power plants make it eligible.
Some reports have suggested that Edison may even purchase the municipal utility, which is expected to face severe challenges in a deregulated market due to its high debt load.
But Brown said Edison has no plans to purchase LADWP.
